minutes.headline: Committee let remote learners play fall sports, halved the high school parking fee, and approved the teachers' MOA.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting during COVID reopening. The committee heard the superintendent's report and an athletics update. It then voted to let remote learners join fall sports, reduce the parking fee, approve the MOA with the teachers' association, and post two stipends. Athletic and facility fees were left unchanged.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to let remote learners take part in the fall 2020 sports season.
The committee approved the memorandum of agreement with the Lunenburg Education Association, 5-0 by roll call.
The committee approved cutting the high school parking fee in half; four members were heard on the roll call and the chair recused.
Athletic and facility fees were left unchanged; facility users will be invoiced for added custodial time.
The committee voted 5-0 to post stipends for technology trainers and a remote learning center coordinator, paid from grants.

why_it_matters: The parking fee cut lowers what high school drivers' families pay, and because that revenue goes to the town general fund, the town budget, mostly taxes, takes in less than the town manager had projected.
The new stipends are funded from federal and COVID relief grants rather than the school operating budget, and the teachers' agreement sets terms for staff during remote and hybrid reopening.
Homeschooled students are not counted in the October 1 enrollment, which sets next year's state aid, so rising homeschooling can reduce that aid.
